newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan and Israel launch expanded air flights.
newsitem.headline: Jordan and Israel launch expanded air flights.

text.p: Jordan and Israel expanded on Monday air transport links with a new Amman-Haifa air route and an extra flight between Amman and Tel Aviv.

A Jordanian 50 seater turbo-prop Canadian Dash plane owned by Royal Wings, a subsidiary of state carrier Royal Jordanian (RJ), flew to Haifa airport, launching the twice-weekly flight for each country, airline sources said.

Airline officials said an extra sixth flight between Tel Aviv and Amman flown by Royal Wings was also launched on Monday, in line with a joint transport accord agreed January 1996. Israel's mainly domestic carrier Arkia operates another five flights a week.
Under a clause of the accord, the two sides review traffic and discuss increasing the frequency of flights and passenger traffic on their air route every six months.

Officials said Jordan had proposed the Haifa-Amman route to cash in on the potential of the large Arab minority in Israel, predominantly in northern Israel around the Haifa area. Many have close family ties with Jordanians.
Arab Israelis crossed into Jordan in large numbers since a peace accord between the two countries in 1994 that ended a 46-year state of war.
Public and tourist buses and privately owned cars have started to cross the border and a recently amended cargo transport accord is expected to ease bureaucratic hurdles to cross border trade.
